info.name: Cloudflare Worker - health and webhook simulation
info.description:
Tests the Worker directly. Requests 1, 2, 3 and 5 involve no Autotask and write nothing anywhere, so they work even while the Autotask side is blocked.

SETUP
  workerBaseUrl        https://autotask-abillity-sync.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev
                       (no trailing slash)
  webhookToken         the WebhookToken secret you set on the Worker
  syncFlagUdfLabel     must match the Worker's AutotaskSyncFlagUdfLabel exactly
  abillityIdUdfLabel   must match the Worker's AutotaskAbillityIdUdfLabel exactly
  testAutotaskCompanyId  any number - only appears in log lines
  testAbillityCompanyId  a real aBILLity company id, used by request 4
  testNewName          the name request 4 will set

ORDER
  1 health check          - is the Worker live and configured?
  2 wrong token           - does it reject properly? (401 is the pass)
  3 simulate, not flagged - safe, writes nothing
  4 simulate, flagged     - WRITES TO aBILLity
  5 deactivation callback - logs only

Open the Worker's log stream first (Cloudflare > your Worker > Logs > Begin log
stream). These requests are only half the story - the log is the other half.

Requests 3 and 4 send the payload shape Autotask really sends, captured from a live
webhook: EntityType "Account", Fields as an object keyed by field name, and a picklist
UDF carrying the selected value's numeric id rather than its label.

syncFlagYesValue must be the picklist value id that means yes, and the Worker needs the
same id in its AutotaskSyncFlagYesValues variable.

request.description:
Proves the Worker is deployed, configured and that your token matches. Involves no Autotask and no aBILLity.

Reports only WHETHER each setting is present, never its value.

Run this before anything else - if it fails, nothing downstream can work.

exec: console.log('Worker is live and configured. Check the two UDF labels above match');
console.log('Autotask exactly - capitals and spacing included.');
console.log('Token mismatch: {{webhookToken}} is not the WebhookToken secret.');
console.log('The URL registered in Autotask will have the same problem.');
console.log('A variable or secret is missing - the body above names which.');
console.log('404 - the deployed Worker predates /health. Redeploy src/index.js.');

item.name: 2. Health check with a wrong token (expect 401)

request.description:
Confirms the Worker actually rejects a bad token - that the auth check works rather than letting everything through.

A 401 here is the PASS.

exec: pm.test('Bad token is rejected', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(401); });

item.name: 3. Simulate a webhook - NOT flagged for sync (safe)

request.description:
Sends a real-shaped Autotask payload with the sync flag set to a value that is NOT your yes value.

Safe: the Worker should skip it, so NOTHING is written to aBILLity. It still exercises routing, the token check, JSON parsing and the flag logic.

This is the payload shape Autotask actually sends - EntityType "Account", Fields as an object, and the flag as a picklist value id.

Expect 200, and in the Worker log:
  Request: POST /api/CompanyNameSync
  ... is not flagged for aBILLity sync ... - skipping

exec: console.log('Worker log should show: "is not flagged for aBILLity sync ... skipping"');
console.log('Nothing should have changed in aBILLity.');

item.name: 4. Simulate a webhook - flagged, real sync (WRITES TO aBILLITY)

request.description:
The same real-shaped payload with the sync flag set to your yes value, so the Worker performs the real aBILLity rename.

*** THIS RENAMES A COMPANY IN aBILLity - LIVE BILLING DATA. ***

syncFlagYesValue must match what the Worker accepts: for a picklist UDF that is the value's numeric id, and the Worker needs the same id in its AutotaskSyncFlagYesValues variable.

Expect 200 and 'Synced company ... ->' in the Worker log.

exec: console.log('Accepted. The Worker log says whether aBILLity actually took it:');
console.log('  "is flagged for sync but has no ..." = the id was blank');
console.log('Confirm with request 1 of the aBILLity collection - check LastUpdated.');
console.log('The Worker reached aBILLity and aBILLity refused.');
console.log('The Worker log has the status and response body.');
pm.test('Worker accepted the webhook', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

request.description:
The endpoint Autotask calls if it ever deactivates the webhook. It only logs.

Writes nothing anywhere. Expect 200 and 'Autotask webhook deactivated: ...' in the log.

variable.value: Worker Test - safe to rename back
